title: Total lifting squares reduce to a fibre by adjunction
statement:
Let $\mathcal B$ be an ordinary category [def-nagata-category] and let $s\mapsto M_s$ be a strict contravariant diagram of categories: a map $r:s\to t$ gives $r^*:M_t\to M_s$, with $(qr)^*=r^*q^*$ and $1^*=1$. Assume each $r^*$ has a left adjoint $r_!$, with a natural Hom bijection $\Phi_r:\operatorname{Hom}(r_!P,Q)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P,r^*Q)$. Define its total category to have objects $(s,P)$, arrows $(r,z):(s,P)\to(t,Q)$ with $z:P\to r^*Q$, and composition $(q,z')(r,z)=(qr,r^*z'\circ z)$. Let a commuting square have left arrow $(f,v):(s,A)\to(t,B)$, right arrow $(g,w):(u,X)\to(v_0,Y)$, top arrow $(a,\alpha)$ and bottom arrow $(b,\beta)$. Thus $ga=bf$ and $a^*w\circ\alpha=f^*\beta\circ v$. Fix $h:t\to u$ with $hf=a$ and $gh=b$. Put $u_f=\Phi_f^{-1}(v)$, $\widetilde\alpha=\Phi_h^{-1}(\Phi_f^{-1}(\alpha)):h_!f_!A\to X$, and $\widetilde\beta=\Phi_h^{-1}(\beta):h_!B\to g^*Y$, using $a^*=f^*h^*$ and $b^*=h^*g^*$. Then
$$w\widetilde\alpha=\widetilde\beta\circ h_!u_f.$$
Moreover $d\mapsto\Phi_h^{-1}(d)$ is a bijection between total diagonals over $h$, namely $d:B\to h^*X$ with $f^*d\circ v=\alpha$ and $h^*w\circ d=\beta$, and fibre diagonals $\delta:h_!B\to X$ with $\delta\circ h_!u_f=\widetilde\alpha$ and $w\delta=\widetilde\beta$. Its inverse is $\delta\mapsto\Phi_h(\delta)$. No model structure, injectivity of base maps or equivalence of the adjoints is assumed.

source.place: Haugseng, Proposition 4.25, proof of the lifting assertion in Section 4.3. This isolates the ordinary total-to-fibre square comparison used there; the statement gives its precise adjunction equations. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag supplies this particular comparison.

proof.text: Write $\alpha_f=\Phi_f^{-1}(\alpha):f_!A\to h^*X$. The strict identities $a^*=f^*h^*$ and $b^*=h^*g^*$ identify the given square equation with $f^*h^*w\circ\alpha=f^*\beta\circ v$. The equation $hf=a$ and the definition of $u_f$ make all displayed composites well typed.

Naturality of the inverse adjunction bijection for $f_!\dashv f^*$ gives $\Phi_f^{-1}(f^*d\circ v)=d\circ\Phi_f^{-1}(v)=d\circ u_f$ for every $d:B\to h^*X$. Since $\Phi_f^{-1}(\alpha)=\alpha_f$ and $\Phi_f^{-1}$ is bijective, the total diagonal condition $f^*d\circ v=\alpha$ is equivalent to $d\circ u_f=\alpha_f$.

Apply $\Phi_f$ to the two maps $h^*w\circ\alpha_f$ and $\beta\circ u_f$ from $f_!A$ to $h^*g^*Y$. Their images are respectively $f^*h^*w\circ\alpha=a^*w\circ\alpha$ and $f^*\beta\circ v$. The commutativity hypothesis therefore implies $h^*w\circ\alpha_f=\beta\circ u_f$, since $\Phi_f$ is bijective.

By definition $\widetilde\alpha=\Phi_h^{-1}(\alpha_f)$ and $\widetilde\beta=\Phi_h^{-1}(\beta)$. Naturality of $\Phi_h$ sends $w\circ\widetilde\alpha$ to $h^*w\circ\alpha_f$ and sends $\widetilde\beta\circ h_!u_f$ to $\beta\circ u_f$. Step 3 and injectivity of $\Phi_h$ give $w\widetilde\alpha=\widetilde\beta\circ h_!u_f$.

For a total diagonal $d:B\to h^*X$, put $\delta=\Phi_h^{-1}(d)$. If $f^*d\circ v=\alpha$, Step 2 gives $d\circ u_f=\alpha_f$. Naturality of $\Phi_h$ then gives $\Phi_h(\delta\circ h_!u_f)=d\circ u_f=\Phi_h(\widetilde\alpha)$, hence $\delta\circ h_!u_f=\widetilde\alpha$.

The other total diagonal equation $h^*w\circ d=\beta$ is, by naturality of $\Phi_h$, exactly $\Phi_h(w\circ\delta)=\Phi_h(\widetilde\beta)$. Since $\Phi_h$ is injective, it yields $w\circ\delta=\widetilde\beta$.

Conversely, let $\delta:h_!B\to X$ satisfy $\delta\circ h_!u_f=\widetilde\alpha$ and $w\circ\delta=\widetilde\beta$, and set $d=\Phi_h(\delta):B\to h^*X$. Applying $\Phi_h$ to the first fibre equation gives $d\circ u_f=\alpha_f$; applying $\Phi_h$ to the second gives $h^*w\circ d=\beta$. Apply $\Phi_f$ to the equality $d\circ u_f=\alpha_f$. Naturality and $\Phi_f(u_f)=v$ identify its left side with $f^*d\circ v$, while $\Phi_f(\alpha_f)=\alpha$ identifies its right side with $\alpha$. Hence $f^*d\circ v=\alpha$.

The two constructions are inverse because $\Phi_h^{-1}(\Phi_h(\delta))=\delta$ and $\Phi_h(\Phi_h^{-1}(d))=d$. Thus $d\mapsto\Phi_h^{-1}(d)$ is the asserted bijection between total and fibre diagonals, with inverse $\delta\mapsto\Phi_h(\delta)$.

lean.statement: theorem adjunctionSquareLifts {B : Type u} [Category.{v} B] (D : Bᵒᵖ ⥤ Cat.{vₘ, uₘ}) (L : ∀ {s t : B}, (s ⟶ t) → (D.obj (op s) ⥤ D.obj (op t))) (adj : ∀ {s t : B} (r : s ⟶ t), L r ⊣ (D.map r.op).toFunctor) {s t z v₀ : B} {A : D.obj (op s)} {B₁ : D.obj (op t)} {X : D.obj (op z)} {Y : D.obj (op v₀)} (f : s ⟶ t) (g : z ⟶ v₀) (h : t ⟶ z) (a : s ⟶ z) (b : t ⟶ v₀) (ha : f ≫ h = a) (hb : h ≫ g = b) (v : A ⟶ (D.map f.op).toFunctor.obj B₁) (w : X ⟶ (D.map g.op).toFunctor.obj Y) (α : A ⟶ (D.map a.op).toFunctor.obj X) (β : B₁ ⟶ (D.map b.op).toFunctor.obj Y) (_hsquare : adjunctionSquareComponent D f h a ha α ≫ (D.map f.op).toFunctor.map ((D.map h.op).toFunctor.map w) = v ≫ (D.map f.op).toFunctor.map (adjunctionSquareComponent D h g b hb β)) : adjunctionSquareTop (adj f) (adj h) (adjunctionSquareComponent D f h a ha α) ≫ w = (L h).map (((adj f).homEquiv A B₁).symm v) ≫ ((adj h).homEquiv B₁ ((D.map g.op).toFunctor.obj Y)).symm (adjunctionSquareComponent D h g b hb β) ∧ ∃ e : {d : B₁ ⟶ (D.map h.op).toFunctor.obj X // v ≫ (D.map f.op).toFunctor.map d = adjunctionSquareComponent D f h a ha α ∧ d ≫ (D.map h.op).toFunctor.map w = adjunctionSquareComponent D h g b hb β} ≃ {δ : (L h).obj B₁ ⟶ X // (L h).map (((adj f).homEquiv A B₁).symm v) ≫ δ = adjunctionSquareTop (adj f) (adj h) (adjunctionSquareComponent D f h a ha α) ∧ δ ≫ w = ((adj h).homEquiv B₁ ((D.map g.op).toFunctor.obj Y)).symm (adjunctionSquareComponent D h g b hb β)}, (∀ d, (e d).val = ((adj h).homEquiv B₁ X).symm d.val) ∧ (∀ δ, (e.symm δ).val = (adj h).homEquiv B₁ X δ.val)
